title: Autoscaler: blend reactive signals with predictive forecast (confidence gating + guardrails)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Dedicated autoscaling policies with customer bounds
content:
Context
We now have (a) hard min/max bounds enforcement in the fleet autoscaler and policy engine, and (b) an MVP forecast service emitting short-horizon demand + confidence. This ticket implements the actual scaling decision logic to blend reactive demand estimation with forecasted demand while keeping customer spend predictable (max bound is strict) and minimizing latency spikes (pre-scale when we trust the forecast).

Goals
- Use forecast to pre-scale Dedicated pools ahead of demand ramps.
- Gate forecast impact by confidence + data quality, and degrade gracefully to reactive-only.
- Add guardrails to avoid overshoot and oscillation, especially during bursty/anomalous traffic.
- Ensure bounds remain strict: final desired replicas MUST be clamped to [min, max].

Non-goals
- Changing the forecast model (handled in ENG-2844).
- Cross-pool cost optimization or fleet-wide arbitrage (out of scope for initial release).

Decision inputs
Reactive signals (existing):
- queue depth + arrival rate trend
- GPU utilization
- p95 end-to-end latency
- throttles / admission control events
- scale lag / provisioning lead time hints (per GPU type)

Predictive signals (new):
- forecasted demand per pool over short horizon (target: 5–15 min)
- forecast confidence score in [0, 1]
- signal freshness timestamp (staleness detection)
- optional: scheduled event flag (when available)

Proposed algorithm (implementation detail; see ADR-0143 for rationale)
1) Compute reactive desired replicas (R):
   - existing reactive controller produces desired count based on queue depth, utilization, and latency SLO pressure.

2) Compute forecast desired replicas (F):
   - translate forecasted QPS/token-rate to required replicas using:
     - per-pool capacity model (tokens/sec per replica) + safety factor
     - known provisioning lead time (don’t request more than we can realistically acquire within horizon)

3) Confidence gating
   - Define thresholds:
     - conf_low: below this, ignore forecast entirely (fallback to reactive)
     - conf_high: above this, allow forecast to pre-scale aggressively (within max)
     - between low/high: blend with reduced weight and additional margin
   - Hard checks that force fallback-to-reactive:
     - forecast stale beyond max_staleness
     - missing required features or NaN/invalid outputs
     - “anomaly” indicator (e.g., >X sigma jump vs recent demand without corroborating queue depth)

4) Blending rule
   - Compute blended desired (B) using a conservative max-based rule rather than averaging:
     - baseline: B = max(R, F_adj)
     - F_adj applies confidence-weighted safety margin and a cap on forecast-driven step size
   - Rationale: avoid forecast pulling us down (scale-down stays reactive + cooldown-driven); forecast is primarily used as a floor for scale-up.

5) Guardrails (overshoot + oscillation)
   - Step limits:
     - limit forecast-driven scale-up per interval (e.g., +N replicas or +X% whichever smaller)
   - Cooldowns:
     - respect existing scale-up cooldown for repeated requests; ensure forecast does not re-trigger scale-up every tick on minor forecast jitter
     - scale-down remains governed by reactive signals + scale-down cooldown; forecast should not trigger scale-down
   - “No ping-pong”:
     - if we scaled up due to forecast within last T minutes and reactive signals do not confirm, require conf_high to scale further
   - Provisioning reality check:
     - if region/hardware supply constraint prevents acquiring capacity, autoscaler should emit “capacity_unavailable” and not continuously increase requested replicas beyond what the actuation path can satisfy

6) Bounds enforcement (must remain strict)
   - Final desired replicas D:
     - D = clamp(B, min_bound, max_bound)
   - We must log whether clamping occurred and why:
     - clamp_reason = min_bound | max_bound | none
     - decision_mode = reactive_only | forecast_gated | forecast_blended | forecast_forced_off

7) Fallback behavior
   - On forecast failure (service down/timeouts), continue reactive-only. Do not page on single pool failure; rely on SLOs for forecast freshness/error rates (ENG-2846 / SRE doc).

Implementation notes
- Extend autoscaler decision struct to carry both R and F (and relevant metadata) so we can:
  - expose decision metrics without high cardinality
  - emit structured logs for audit trail (Console work in ENG-2847)
- Ensure determinism in evaluation:
  - same inputs -> same decision (important for golden tests; policy engine config already deterministic)
- Protect metrics cardinality:
  - avoid tagging metrics with pool_id directly; use sampling + structured logs for per-pool drill-down

Acceptance criteria
- Functional
  - When forecast confidence >= conf_high and forecast implies higher capacity than reactive, autoscaler scales up earlier than reactive-only would, subject to scale-rate limits and max bound.
  - When forecast confidence < conf_low OR forecast is stale/invalid, autoscaler behaves equivalently to reactive-only (no forecast impact).
  - Forecast never triggers scale-down directly.
  - Final desired replicas always respects min/max bounds (0 bound violations).

- Safety/guardrails
  - Demonstrate (in simulation or load test) no persistent oscillation introduced by forecast jitter when confidence is mid/low.
  - Demonstrate overshoot protection: forecast spikes do not cause runaway scaling beyond step limits.

- Observability
  - Decision logs include: R, F, confidence, decision_mode, clamp_reason, and a short reason string suitable for Console.
  - Metrics emitted to support SRE alerts (see ENG-2846): forecast_used counter, fallback_to_reactive counter, forecast_staleness gauge, decision_mode breakdown.

Testing plan
- Unit tests
  - confidence gating behavior at boundaries
  - stale/invalid forecast -> reactive-only
  - clamp behavior at min/max
  - cooldown + step-limit interactions

- Integration tests
  - load profile with scheduled ramp: confirm pre-scale happens when confidence high
  - sudden spike anomaly: confirm step limit + confidence gating prevents overshoot
  - forecast service timeout: ensure autoscaler continues and logs fallback

Links
- ADR-0143 Predictive signal blending (Confluence): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0143-predictive-signal-blending.json
- Architecture: autoscaler bounds + forecasting: sources/confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/autoscaler-bounds-and-forecasting-architecture.json
- Dependent PRs:
  - PR-21941 forecast ingestion scaffolding
  - PR-21966 predictive blending implementation

Rollout
- Behind bounded autoscaling feature flag + design-partner allowlist (ENG-2848).
- Start with dogfood pools in us-east + eu-west; then 2 design partners.
- If any elevated oscillation or scaling lag regressions: disable forecast usage (keep bounds enforcement on).
comments: 2026-01-12 (Keiko Yamamoto): Drafted blending approach based on ADR-0143: forecast should only raise the scale-up floor, never pull down. Next: finalize confidence thresholds + step limits with SRE to avoid paging storms.

2026-01-16 (Sean Gallagher): Please make sure we can answer “why did we scale” without exploding metric cardinality. Prefer structured logs with sampling, plus a low-cardinality metric for decision_mode and clamp_reason. Also: define staleness threshold explicitly (we’ve been bitten by stale predictors).

2026-01-20 (Keiko Yamamoto): Implemented gating checks: stale (>10m), invalid, timeout -> forecast_forced_off. Added mid-confidence mode with extra safety margin and capped step size. Scale-down path unchanged (reactive + cooldown).

2026-01-24 (Vanessa Ortiz): Fleet note: don’t request more than actuation can realistically place in region during constrained supply. If we repeatedly hit ‘capacity unavailable’, we should surface it clearly to Console/audit trail so customers understand why performance may degrade despite a high max.
2026-02-02 (Keiko Yamamoto): Open question: conf thresholds defaults. Proposal: conf_low=0.35, conf_high=0.70. Mid band uses reduced weight + +15% safety margin. Will tune after canary runs.

2026-02-06 (Allison Grant): For audit trail, please include a single summary field (e.g., reason_summary) with stable phrases; we can map that cleanly in Console. Also log both R and F so we can reconstruct disagreements during incidents.

2026-02-10 (Keiko Yamamoto): PR up: sources/github/redwood/pr-21966.json. Includes unit tests + integration test harness for ramp and anomaly profiles. Added decision_mode and clamp_reason to structured logs; metrics are low-cardinality.

2026-02-13 (Rafael Mendes): Ran through staging with replayed traffic. Looks good overall; one edge: repeated forecast_high updates can still scale up every tick if step limit is too high. Please ensure step limit is small enough (and/or cooldown applies) to prevent runaways.

2026-02-14 (Keiko Yamamoto): Adjusted scale-up cooldown interaction: forecast-driven scale-up now respects the same cooldown gate as reactive scale-up. Step limit reduced from +50% to +25% per interval by default; override only via advanced settings.
2026-02-18 (Connor O'Brien): Marking Done. Will roll out behind allowlist with ENG-2848. Please coordinate with ENG-2849 load tests for final thresholds before enabling for design partners.
